To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

MI/R induces the expression of P-selectins, E-selectin and ICAM- 1 in the mouse heart and that the genetic deficiency of these adhesion molecules attenuate PMN sequestrations and subsequent myocardial injury.

P-selectin (alpha-granule membrane glycoprotein 140), E-selectin (endoglycan), and intercellulr cell adhesion molecule-1 (ICAM) are upregulated after myocardial infarction and that genetic deficiency of these molecules attenuates polymorphonuclear (PMN) infiltration and myocardial injury.

P-selectin (alpha-GP40), ICAM-1 and E-selectin are expressed on endothelial cells in mice during reperfusion after myocardial ischemia, and that deficiencies of these molecules and CD18 attenuate myocardial neutrophil infiltration and injury after in vivo myocardial ischemia and reperfusion in mice.
